items.title: James "Sugarboy" Crawford Interview, 1975-04-29
items.q: And Tommy Ridgely, he said he wanted some help. He's still playing. So, he asked me about helping him out. I gave him some of my arrangements, maybe coming to the rehearsal, you know, if we had time. So, I ended up playing with him. I ended up playing piano with him.

ctx.x: I'll talk about it. I'll talk about it. I'll talk about it. I'll talk about it. You should have, you could have gotten the bundle. You could have gotten the bundle. I'll just talk that out. I'll talk about it. I'll talk about it.

Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Until, let's see, around 60 with my band. Until around 67. Yeah. And then around the end of 67, I started playing with Tommy Ridgely. I stopped playing with my band. I said, well, I'm going to give it up. I wasn't making no money. So, I gave it up. And Tommy Ridgely, he said he wanted some help. He's still playing.
